question.text: Surya Capital is structuring its new Cat II AIF and is considering appointing its group company 'Surya Custody Services Ltd.' (a SEBI-registered custodian) as the fund's custodian. As per SEBI (AIF) (Amendment) Regulations 2024, this is:

answer.text: Permitted automatically because both entities have the same SEBI registrations.
Permitted ONLY if specific conditions laid down by SEBI are fulfilled; otherwise the custodian shall not be a related party to the sponsor/manager/designated partners.
Permitted only for Cat III AIFs.

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook (page 115) states that the custodian shall not be a related party to the sponsors or designated partners unless specific conditions laid down by SEBI are fulfilled. This is therefore a conditional permission, not an outright prohibition or an automatic permission. The Trap: Option A is over-absolute. Option B ignores the related-party filter that applies unless the specified conditions are met. Option D invents a category-specific carve-out. Note: The exact conditions that must be fulfilled are those prescribed by SEBI; candidates should refer to the conditions as laid down by SEBI rather than relying on additional governance/disclosure conditions not stated in the workbook.
